title: Only half of the round help button is on screen, so the part you can tap is about half the finger size
what: The floating Help and feedback button is 48 points wide but sits half behind the screen edge, so only about 24 points of it can be touched, right on the edge where Android's back swipe lives. Moving it needs a drag, which a screen-reader user cannot do.
expected: The part of the button you can touch is at least the app's own 48-point finger size, away from the back-swipe edge, and it can be moved without dragging (or hidden from Settings, which exists).
how_often: every time they tap the help button
fix_line: Let more of the tab show, or give it a touch area that reaches into the screen

title: The Undo bar runs out after 6 seconds even for a member using a screen reader
what: After a delete the Undo bar stays 6 seconds and only stops its clock while a finger rests on it. A screen-reader user has to swipe to reach it, and the clock keeps running; the phone's own 'time to take action' setting is not used. On iPhone the bar is not even read out, since the announcement used works on Android only.
expected: With a screen reader on, the Undo stays until it is reached (or for the phone's chosen time), and it is read out on both phones.
who: members who use a screen reader
fix_line: Make the Undo wait longer or stay while a screen reader is on, and announce it

title: The gym sync sign-in form cannot be filled in reliably with a screen reader
what: The Email, Password, Gym code and Name boxes have no spoken name, so once typed in a screen reader reads only what is in them. The 'Create account / Sign in' choice is not said to be a choice and does not say which one is picked, and is smaller than finger size. The agreement tick box is not said to be a tick box and never says if it is ticked.
expected: Every box says what it is for, the choice says which one is picked, and the tick box says ticked or not ticked.
who: members who use a screen reader
how_often: every time (feature is behind a switch)
fix_line: Give each box a spoken name and give the choice and tick box their proper roles and states

title: When a backup, restore, gym connect or erase fails, a screen reader says nothing
what: Several Settings cards show their failure only as small red words placed under the buttons, with no spoken announcement, although the app's own rule is that error lines are read out. A screen-reader user taps the button and hears no result.
expected: Every failure line in these cards is read out when it appears, like the app's shared error line.
who: members who use a screen reader
fix_line: Use the shared error line that is read out in these cards

title: Closing the feedback sheet while speaking throws away what was said
what: If the sheet is closed (a tap outside, the back button) while recording or while the voice is being turned into text, the recording is deleted and the words never reach the box. Typed words are kept when the sheet opens again, spoken ones are not.
expected: Words already spoken are still turned into text and waiting in the box when the sheet opens again, or the member is asked before they are thrown away.
fix_line: Finish turning the clip into text and keep it with the unsent message

title: The AI key box and its Edit button do not say what they are for
what: The box for typing your own AI key has no spoken name, and its button only says 'Edit', so a screen-reader user does not know what is being edited.
expected: The box and button say 'AI key' in their spoken names.
who: members who use a screen reader
how_often: every time (feature is behind a switch)
fix_line: Give the box and the Edit button spoken names that mention the AI key
